scope: Bridger design research: generic runtime, Effect v4, Alchemy, FoldKit, ERP requirements

effect_unstable_policy.scope: All Effect v4 unstable features are eligible; maturity is not an exclusion or separate approval gate
effect_unstable_policy.version_policy: Use pinned release imports and validate compatibility

limitations: Repository versions, not verified npm dist-tags
Proposed uses are not implemented features
Odoo Context7 snippets had version-mismatched links; Odoo claims use direct 19.0 source inspection
tag_method: Keyword-derived retrieval aids, not reviewed classifications

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Describe activation, service calls and typed operational failures; preserve cleanup defects in host diagnostics.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Typed error channels do not prevent arbitrary JavaScript defects or prove business correctness.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Shared contracts package for plugin services; request-scoped tenant, actor and locale environments.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. TypeScript types erase at runtime; runtime-loaded modules need manifest/schema checks and matching service identities.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Build activation dependency environments and share intended infrastructure layers.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Layer graph construction is not a dynamic plugin resolver; memo-map ownership must match activation lifetimes.

entries.title: Resource ownership and finalization: `Scope`, acquire/release operations

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: One scope per activation, nested scopes per call, deterministic cleanup of connections and handlers.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Closing a scope does not undo committed database writes or external actions.

entries.title: Structured concurrency and interruption: fibers and scoped forks

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Tie background plugin workers to activation lifetime; coordinate cancellation on removal.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Choose fork ownership deliberately; detached work and uninterruptible operations can outlive intended teardown.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Rebuild a credential-dependent connector or service generation while existing users finish.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Invalidation does not revoke already borrowed contexts. This is useful evidence for leases, not a complete hot-replacement protocol.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Cache tenant or regional connector environments with idle release.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Tenant selection and authorization remain application rules; bound resource cardinality.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Candidate primitives underneath leased provider generations.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Reference counting alone does not block new leases, validate plugin dependencies, or order dependent shutdown.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Deduplicate expensive connector acquisition with bounded entries and cleanup on eviction.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Cached ownership differs from borrowed ownership; do not assume eviction is safe for escaped handles.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Candidate mechanism for refreshed configuration or replaceable scoped values.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core exports verified. Recheck current replacement/failure semantics before choosing over E06–E08.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: One application-owned execution boundary for React, imperative integrations and command entry points.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core export verified. Runtime disposal and plugin removal are separate ownership operations.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Represent provider-consumer edges, inspect topology and export diagnostic diagrams.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Bridger still defines edge meanings, optional dependencies, cycles and teardown policy.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Atomically update related host registry state and generation counters.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Transactions retry on conflict; they do not enlist SQL, files or remote APIs. Avoid non-repeatable external effects inside them.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Evaluate atomic coordination between host state and local notifications.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core exports verified. Process-local structures are neither a durable event log nor a distributed lock.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Let tenants share bounded database/import capacity without one busy tenant monopolizing released permits.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. This bounds concurrent work in one runtime; it is not a global throughput quota.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Implement host snapshots and lifecycle subscriptions consumed by FoldKit/React adapters.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Publishes initial state and committed updates; remote reconnection, replay IDs and UI scheduling remain adapter work.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: CSV imports, report exports, change feeds and bounded plugin event fan-out.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core exports. Choose buffering and slow-consumer policy; local PubSub has no durable delivery guarantee.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Batch record lookups across rich screens and avoid N+1 service calls.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Include tenant, authorization scope and consistency requirements in request/cache identity.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Backoff for imports/connectors and scheduled maintenance.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core exports. An in-memory schedule does not survive process loss; write idempotent jobs and decide distributed ownership.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Switch among approved email, document extraction or integration providers with explicit attempt policy.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Fallback after ambiguous remote success can duplicate an action; use operation IDs and reconciliation.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Validate manifests, configuration, commands and imported data; distinguish encoded transport shapes from domain values.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Successful decoding does not authorize a command or enforce cross-record invariants.

entries.title: Schema-derived JSON Schema, formatters, equivalence, optics and differs

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Reuse contract metadata for API docs, validation messages and form/update tooling.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core capabilities. UI layout, permissions and workflow semantics require explicit metadata; arbitrary transformations are not portable JSON Schema.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Evaluate serializable field catalogs and compiler tooling for installed module contracts.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core export. Opaque checks need representation identities/handlers; serializing a schema is not serializing arbitrary executable code.

entries.title: Variant models and schema compilation: `Model`, `VariantSchema`, AOT/JIT compilers from `effect/schema`

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Explore distinct insert/update/read shapes and compile expensive validation paths after measurement.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. Keep compiler and persistence details behind adapters; confirm deployment/CSP compatibility for JIT.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Foundation for quantities, prices and exchange calculations without binary floating-point representation.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. Define currency, scale, rounding stage/mode and SQL/JSON encoding explicitly; no accounting rules are supplied.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Distinguish timestamps, durations and zone-aware scheduling.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core. DateTime represents an instant; date-only accounting periods and local calendar dates need their own model.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Prevent accidental ID mixing and describe selective form/document updates.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core exports. Branded types do not validate unknown input; patches need field-level authorization and concurrency checks.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Typed plugin config and connector credentials that resist accidental default printing.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core exports. Redaction is not encryption, secret storage, access control or protection against malicious trusted code.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Transactional domain commands; nested transaction support is implemented using connection transaction controls/savepoints.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. Requires driver, database isolation choices, tenant enforcement and integration tests; external effects are outside the SQL transaction.

entries.title: SQL schemas, models and batched resolvers: `SqlSchema`, `SqlModel`, `SqlResolver`

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Typed persistence boundary and batched data retrieval behind ERP repositories.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. This is not an Odoo-style extensible model registry or a complete ORM inheritance system.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Execute versioned schema changes for a deployment or module upgrade.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. Bridger/ERP must specify locking, expand/contract changes, backups, compatibility windows and upgrade failure recovery.

entries.title: Persistent caches, queues and rate limiting: `effect/persistence`

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Cache remote metadata, buffer integration work and enforce connector quotas.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. Verify backend durability, acknowledgement and retry semantics; presence of PersistedQueue alone is not an exactly-once guarantee.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Model procurement approvals, document processing and long-running fulfillment with schema-defined payloads/results and deterministic execution identities.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. Persistence depends on engine choice; pin code/schema versions for outstanding workflows.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Isolate resumable steps and remote calls within a workflow.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. External side effects still require idempotency and handling for success-before-recording crash windows.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Wait for human approval, a webhook or a deadline without treating an ordinary sleeping fiber as durable storage.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. Define authorization, event correlation, timeout and duplicate-response behavior at the application boundary.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Describe compensating business actions when a multi-step process fails.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. Compensation is not rollback. Source explicitly limits compensation finalizers to top-level workflow effects, excluding nested activities.

entries.title: Cluster entities, sharding and workflow engine: `effect/cluster`

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Evaluate distributed ownership of account/order actors and durable workflow execution across workers.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. Distribution is an optional infrastructure choice; rolling upgrades, fencing and message/storage semantics need a failure model.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Explore append/replay/synchronization infrastructure and event projections.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. Do not assume it is a legally sufficient audit ledger or a complete event-sourced ERP. Define ordering, conflict resolution, retention and authorization separately.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Integration connectors, attachment transfer and incoming webhooks using Effect resource/error conventions.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. Platform server layers and deployment support must be selected separately.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Share endpoint contracts, generated clients, OpenAPI documentation and middleware between modules.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. Dynamic installation requires an explicit route-registration seam and collision/removal policy.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Typed service boundaries between browser, server and workers.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. Typed protocol definitions are not authentication or cross-version negotiation; verify transport and streaming contracts.

entries.title: Reactive atoms, resource results and API adapters: `effect/reactivity`

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Evaluate UI data caching/invalidation and remote result state alongside Bridger lifecycle snapshots.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. FoldKit already has its own state/update model; choose a single owner for each state and bridge subscriptions deliberately.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Correlate plugin activation, generation, tenant and command IDs; inspect failure causes and export telemetry.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Core Logger/Metric/Tracer exports; observability integration requires version review. Telemetry is not the business audit record; avoid high-cardinality labels and sensitive payloads.

entries.title: Controlled time, schema checks and generated test data: `effect/testing`, `Arbitrary`

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Exercise lease-drain timeouts, retry policies, schema round trips and generated module/configuration cases.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Testing exports verified; Arbitrary explicitly unstable. Database races and restart recovery still need integration/fault tests.

fields.Proposed Bridger / ERP use: Optional invoice extraction, assisted search and drafting plugins behind a shared application service.
fields.Maturity and limitation: Unstable. Keep authorization, business validation and human approval outside model discretion; AI is not required by Bridger core.

fields.Verified behavior and source: `Alchemy.Stack` runs an Effect describing resources, providers, state and outputs. [Guide](https://alchemy.run/getting-started/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Compose deployable ERP infrastructure in TypeScript.
fields.Limit or design implication: A stack is a deployment unit; it is not a tenant's active plugin registry.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Resource attributes are typed deferred Outputs; using one as another resource's input creates a graph edge. [Resources](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/resource/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Stable infrastructure IDs per module and explicit dependency ordering.
fields.Limit or design implication: Renaming an identifier can affect physical resource lifecycle.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Outputs model values available after provisioning. [Inputs and outputs](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/outputs/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Wire database addresses, queue URLs and browser API endpoints without manual copying.
fields.Limit or design implication: Keep deploy-time Outputs out of ordinary plugin service contracts.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Lifecycle plans create/update/replace/delete/no-op and invokes convergent reconciliation. [Lifecycle](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/resource-lifecycle/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Review module infrastructure requirements before applying them.
fields.Limit or design implication: Reconciliation is not an atomic business transaction.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Deletion follows reverse dependencies; `RemovalPolicy.retain()` keeps the cloud object while removing its state entry. [Lifecycle](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/resource-lifecycle/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Preserve records and attachments when disabling modules.
fields.Limit or design implication: Retention also forgets management state; it is not a backup or reversible uninstall.

fields.Verified behavior and source: `renamedFrom` records an identity move. [Renaming](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/renaming/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Evolve module packaging without accidental infrastructure replacement.
fields.Limit or design implication: Validate all state addresses and dependency references during a rename.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Providers define reconciliation, diff, deletion and optional read; read can distinguish owned and unowned resources. [Providers](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/provider/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Bring existing ERP infrastructure under deployment management; add vendor integrations.
fields.Limit or design implication: Adoption is provider-specific ownership takeover, not importing ERP data.

fields.Verified behavior and source: CLI exposes `alchemy drift` for detection and optional repair. [Drift](https://alchemy.run/cli/drift/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Detect manual infrastructure changes that invalidate plugin assumptions.
fields.Limit or design implication: Schedule and approve repair independently of runtime activation; verify provider coverage.

fields.Verified behavior and source: State is scoped by stack/stage; local, Cloudflare, Postgres and memory implementations are documented. Postgres uses a session advisory lock per stack/stage. [State](https://alchemy.run/state-store/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Coordinate team deployments and recover provisioning progress.
fields.Limit or design implication: This state is infrastructure metadata, not the ERP database or an install journal.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Separate environment stages and auth profiles are CLI concepts. [Stages](https://alchemy.run/environments/stages/), [CLI](https://alchemy.run/cli/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Preview, development and production environments with explicit deployment identity.
fields.Limit or design implication: Stage separation does not establish row-level tenant isolation.

fields.Verified behavior and source: References read persisted upstream outputs at plan time; borrowers do not own referenced resources. [References](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/references/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Share foundational databases or artifact stores across module deployments.
fields.Limit or design implication: Upstream must already exist; reference resolution does not orchestrate its deployment.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Actions run Effects on changed input hashes; they have no delete/replace lifecycle. [Actions](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/action/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Build artifacts, seed infrastructure or apply controlled deployment work.
fields.Limit or design implication: Removing an Action does not undo its side effects; design idempotence and migration history.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Outer constructors run during planning and cold start; returned handlers run for events. [Phases](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/phases/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Express infrastructure needs alongside service implementations.
fields.Limit or design implication: Plugin activation side effects cannot blindly run in this constructor.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Bindings connect infrastructure to a runtime and provide typed clients; implementations generate native bindings or IAM/env wiring. [Bindings](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/binding/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Host adapters can supply storage or queue capabilities to plugins.
fields.Limit or design implication: Runtime-loaded plugins cannot infer and provision new deployment permissions merely by calling a service.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Effect Layers can encapsulate resources and bindings behind an application service. [Layers](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/layers/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: A strong seam for `Storage`, `Jobs`, `Database` implementations.
fields.Limit or design implication: Keep those deployment Layers distinct from per-activation plugin scopes.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Tag/implementation separation is documented for mutually bound deployed runtimes. [Circular bindings](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/circular-bindings/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Useful for infrastructure topology research.
fields.Limit or design implication: The page still describes create/update hooks while newer lifecycle docs use reconcile; verify source before copying. This does not justify cyclic Bridger activation dependencies.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Config resolved in Construction becomes a runtime binding; `Config.Redacted` uses the secret channel. [Secrets](https://alchemy.run/environments/secrets/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Inject provider credentials without hardcoding them into plugins.
fields.Limit or design implication: Config first read only inside a handler is not discovered for binding; browser configuration must contain no secrets.

fields.Verified behavior and source: `ProviderLayer.dual` switches implementations, with local data-plane routing and scoped process management. [Local provider](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-code/local-provider/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Exercise adapters against emulators while retaining the same contracts.
fields.Limit or design implication: Development hot reload is a different lifecycle from installing a production plugin.

fields.Verified behavior and source: A suite deploys once, tests live resources, then destroys; local mode is also supported. [Testing](https://alchemy.run/testing/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Test queue, database, permissions and deployment contracts that mocks miss.
fields.Limit or design implication: Tests need isolated stages, cleanup and controlled cost; no tests were executed here.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Official CI guidance covers stage-based deployment workflows. [CI](https://alchemy.run/environments/ci/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Review each ERP/module release in an isolated environment.
fields.Limit or design implication: Preview data provisioning and anonymization still require application policy.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Request scopes close per event; instance cleanup on Workers is unavailable and on Lambda is best effort. [Runtime scopes](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/runtime/#instance-scope-vs-request-scope)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Determines where Bridger can keep an in-memory host and lease counters.
fields.Limit or design implication: Cloud eviction is not a graceful `host.remove`; durable business cleanup cannot depend on scope finalization.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Bindings expose cloud events as Effect Streams and wire source/handler infrastructure. [Event sources](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/event-sources/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Inbound integrations, scheduled work and background processing.
fields.Limit or design implication: Persist business events and handle redelivery rather than treating an in-memory subscription as durable delivery.

fields.Verified behavior and source: SQS, SNS and Kinesis sinks expose batch APIs through Effect Sink with generated permissions. [Sinks](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/sinks/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Bulk imports, reporting pipelines and outbound integration events.
fields.Limit or design implication: Batch sizing, partial failures and business idempotency need explicit contracts.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Cloudflare workflow tasks checkpoint results, support retries, rollback callbacks, sleep and event waits. [Workflows](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/workflows/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Purchase approvals, long imports and integration orchestration.
fields.Limit or design implication: Replay requires stable step IDs and serializable values; external writes still need idempotency. Plugin removal must account for running workflow versions.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Effect SQL, Drizzle and Prisma integration paths include existing databases, Postgres and migration guidance. [SQL](https://alchemy.run/sql/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Relational ERP persistence and controlled schema evolution.
fields.Limit or design implication: Migration deployment is not a complete module migration protocol or an ORM extension model.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Cloudflare documents D1/KV/R2/Hyperdrive/Queues/DOs; AWS documents Lambda, S3, SQS, DynamoDB and other services. [Cloudflare](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/), [AWS](https://alchemy.run/aws/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Documents, relational connectivity, caches, jobs and compute.
fields.Limit or design implication: Provider breadth is not semantic interchangeability; choose consistency, transaction and regional behavior explicitly.

fields.Verified behavior and source: OTLP Layers configure signals and destinations; destinations can fan out while preserving span IDs, with stack/stage attributes. [Telemetry](https://alchemy.run/infrastructure-as-effects/telemetry/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Correlate plugin activation, service calls, jobs and infrastructure changes.
fields.Limit or design implication: Add plugin generation, tenant and operation IDs yourself; operational telemetry is not the audit ledger.

fields.Verified behavior and source: `Cloudflare.WorkerLoader` supplies runtime `load`/`get` for source modules in separate isolates. [Worker Loader](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/worker-loader/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: A verified cloud primitive for hot-loaded code, including trusted modules.
fields.Limit or design implication: It needs a Bridger transport adapter; it does not share the host's Effect Context or scopes.

fields.Verified behavior and source: Dispatch namespaces are documented for executing deployed tenant Workers. [Workers for Platforms](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/workers-for-platforms/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Alternative boundary for independently deployed tenant/module execution.
fields.Limit or design implication: Dynamic dispatch and same-process service installation have different lifecycle and latency contracts.

fields.Verified behavior and source: `Cloudflare.Website.Foldkit` supplies Vite deployment and SPA fallback; frontend Effect pinning belongs to the app. [Foldkit integration](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/foldkit/)
fields.Relevance to Bridger / ERP: Deploy the ERP shell and its API address alongside backend infrastructure.
fields.Limit or design implication: Browser bundles cannot access Worker bindings directly; use API routes and design browser module loading separately.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo manifests declare metadata and prerequisite modules. [Module manifests](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/zh_CN/developer/reference/backend/module.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Versioned manifests, publisher identity, artifact digest, compatible host/schema ranges, required/optional services and contribution ownership. Reject incompatible graphs before activation. Administrator approval of trusted code is an application policy.

fields.Vendor evidence: SAP distinguishes key-user, developer and side-by-side extensions. [SAP extensibility](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_CLOUD/0f69f8fb28ac4bf48d2b57b9637e81fa/533228e1e854433ab16d013f161ca509.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Specify separate seams for metadata customization, trusted code plugins and external integrations. Published contracts need compatibility policy and deprecation windows. Avoid requiring internal table access for ordinary extensions.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo has module upgrade scripts and phases. [Upgrade scripts](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/nl/developer/reference/upgrades/upgrade_scripts.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Track artifact availability, schema readiness, tenant enablement and runtime activation separately. Removing an activation must not drop tables or reverse business transactions. Hot-install code does not prove safe online schema migration.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo's ORM supports model inheritance, fields and record caching. [ORM API](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/developer/reference/backend/orm.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Decide typed extension composition, namespaced fields, relation ownership, validation, persisted versus derived fields, dependency invalidation, cycle rejection and query batching. Record schema version must remain intelligible after a plugin is disabled.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo interprets view definitions; SAP exposes custom fields and extension inventory. [Odoo views](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/ar/developer/reference/user_interface/view_architectures.html), [SAP key-user extensibility](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_CLOUD/0f69f8fb28ac4bf48d2b57b9637e81fa/3ccb50e724b045508fea8b2cf1774b2b.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: An ERP UI package owns forms, lists, actions, routes, menus, reports and extension slots. Define deterministic ordering and conflict errors. FoldKit adapts those contributions into Model/Message/update/view; Bridger only owns their availability and lifetime.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo Studio supports ordered steps and exclusive approval. This source is SaaS 19.3. [Approval rules](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/saas-19.3/applications/studio/approval_rules.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Persist transitions, approver identity, policy revision, deadlines and delegation. Enforce approvals server-side, including API calls. Define escalation, cancellation and reassignment if a plugin version retires. Approval must survive process restart.

fields.Vendor evidence: Intacct authenticates company-scoped operations and supports entity context. [Request authentication](https://developer.intacct.com/web-services/requests/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: A platform identity adapter supplies principal, session, tenant, company and delegation. Plan SSO/MFA and service accounts separately. Never let a caller-supplied company identifier substitute for authorization.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo documents model, record and field access; SAP groups application access through roles/catalogs. [Odoo security](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/th/developer/reference/backend/security.html), [SAP business roles](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_CLOUD/a630d57fc5004c6383e7a81efee7a8bb/4236eef12b8b4d4286c53aa89899a6f5.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Define deny-by-default permissions, row/field policies and action checks. Separate payee maintenance, payment approval and payment execution. Enforce the same policy in queries, exports, reports, background jobs and integrations.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo checks cross-company relations and supports company-dependent values. [Multi-company guidelines](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/fr/developer/howtos/company.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Distinguish customer tenant from legal entity, branch and reporting group. Decide database isolation, shared records and tenant plugin sets. Include tenant/company in cache, job and idempotency keys. Trusted in-process plugins share process privileges; scoped services are not a security sandbox.

fields.Vendor evidence: Intacct exposes customers, vendors, items and units. [API domain catalog](https://developer.intacct.com/api/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Establish parties, addresses, products, variants, units and external identifiers as explicit shared contracts. Support merge/alias history without breaking posted documents. Agree which module owns each identity and which consumers may enrich it.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo uses double-entry bookkeeping. [Accounting](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/applications/finance/accounting.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Balanced journal entries, explicit posting commands, period checks, stable numbering, immutable posted representation and linked corrective entries. A posted invoice and its ledger effects must share a deliberate transaction boundary.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo retains company and transaction currency values. [Multi-currency accounting overview](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/applications/finance/accounting.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Use decimal money with currency, documented precision and rounding stage. Snapshot rates and policy revisions on documents. Define residual allocation, gains/losses and historical conversion. Never assume a JavaScript number alone represents money safely.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo packages fiscal rules by country and constrains switching after posting. [Fiscal localizations](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/applications/finance/fiscal_localizations.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Locale packages own effective-dated tax rules, legal document formats, declarations and exchange adapters. Validate each target locale with domain specialists and fixtures; installing a package alone is not compliance evidence. Preserve the rule version used historically.

fields.Vendor evidence: Intacct exposes invoices, bills, payments and aging. [Finance API catalog](https://developer.intacct.com/api/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Partial settlement, credit notes, disputes, due dates, allocations and duplicate detection. Maintain reconciled versus outstanding amounts through atomic transitions. Distinguish invoice state, payment attempt state and settlement state.

fields.Vendor evidence: Intacct includes bank feeds, accounts and transfers. [Cash management catalog](https://developer.intacct.com/api/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Payment providers are adapters with durable requests, external references, webhook verification and reconciliation. An unknown result must remain pending investigation rather than automatically creating a second transfer. No raw payment credentials in plugin logs.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo finance covers assets and analytics; Intacct exposes budgets and allocations. [Odoo finance](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/applications/finance.html), [Intacct ledger catalog](https://developer.intacct.com/api/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Separate asset lifecycle, depreciation policy, budgets, cost centers and analytical dimensions. Version financial report definitions and preserve drill-down to source entries. Local accounting policy remains an explicit selection and validation task.

fields.Vendor evidence: Intacct covers orders and price lists. [Order entry catalog](https://developer.intacct.com/api/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Quote-to-order-to-delivery-to-invoice lineage, price validity, discount approvals, credit limits, returns and CRM handoff. Snapshot accepted commercial terms so later price plugin changes do not rewrite existing orders.

fields.Vendor evidence: Intacct covers purchasing and vendor transactions. [Purchasing catalog](https://developer.intacct.com/api/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Requisitions, RFQs, purchase orders, receipts and invoice matching. Define quantity/price tolerances, supplier approvals and backorders. A three-way matching policy must state its exceptions and authority to override.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo offers reservation timing policies; Intacct exposes warehouses and inventory transactions. [Odoo reservations, SaaS 19.4](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/saas-19.4/nl/applications/inventory_and_mrp/inventory/shipping_receiving/reservation_methods.html), [Intacct inventory catalog](https://developer.intacct.com/api/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Stock movements, reservations, lots/serials, locations, units, counts and returns. Prevent two orders reserving the same availability through database concurrency control. Define negative-stock policy and valuation/posting integration explicitly.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo bills of materials describe components and production operations. [Bill of materials](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/fr/applications/inventory_and_mrp/manufacturing/basic_setup/bill_configuration.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Explore BOM revisions, routings, work centers, capacity, yield, scrap, subcontracting and work-in-progress costing. Quality checks and maintenance are adjacent module proposals needing further domain research. Preserve the production revision actually used.

entries.title: Projects, time, expenses and service delivery

fields.Vendor evidence: Intacct exposes projects, tasks and timesheets. [Project/resource catalog](https://developer.intacct.com/api/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Cost and billable time, expense approvals, rate cards, milestones and resource calendars. Define corrections after billing and avoid charging one time entry twice. Plan field service/helpdesk as optional extensions with their own process research.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo payroll has locale-specific modules. [Payroll localizations](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/applications/hr/payroll/payroll_localizations.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Separate personnel records, leave, schedules, payroll calculations and payment exports. Use effective-dated contracts and restricted fields. Payroll rules and retention require validation for every supported locale; no universal payroll claim.

fields.Vendor evidence: Intacct exposes contract billing/revenue schedules. [Contract catalog](https://developer.intacct.com/api/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Separate recurring billing from revenue recognition, usage metering, amendments and entitlements. Contract revisions need deterministic effective dates and replay rules. Recognition policy must be validated for the applicable reporting regime.

fields.Vendor evidence: Intacct distinguishes domestic and global consolidation. [Consolidation catalog](https://developer.intacct.com/api/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Explicit paired intercompany documents, ownership structures, elimination rules, currency translation and consolidation runs. Reconcile rather than silently repair mismatches. Scope this as an advanced finance package, with a separate acceptance dataset.

fields.Vendor evidence: Intacct distinguishes request correlation from duplicate suppression and offers transaction grouping. [XML request semantics](https://developer.intacct.com/web-services/requests/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Version API/event schemas, outbox/inbox records, deduplication keys, retry categories and dead-letter recovery. Domain mutation plus outbox insertion must be atomic. A successful retry mechanism does not establish exactly-once business effects. New Intacct adapters should investigate REST independently.

fields.Vendor evidence: SAP provides migration objects and staging/direct migration approaches. [SAP data migration](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_CLOUD/d5699934e7004d048c4801b552f3b013/4c4047f1989f4b9a836dbc24f82989e8.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Staging validation, field mapping, external IDs, dry run, resumable batches and per-row errors. Reconcile opening balances and quantities to control totals before activation. Keep business data import distinct from module schema upgrades.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo search views filter records; Intacct supports data delivery for analytics. [Odoo search architecture](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/ar/developer/reference/user_interface/view_architectures.html), [Intacct DDS catalog](https://developer.intacct.com/api/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Authorized query contracts, pagination, saved filters, export jobs, report snapshots and searchable projections. Record index lag and report consistency point. Search must not expose hidden records or field snippets. Translation/timezone formatting belongs to presentation contracts.

fields.Vendor evidence: Intacct has an attachment API. [Attachments](https://developer.intacct.com/api/company-console/attachments/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Object storage with record authorization, metadata, checksums, versions, upload limits and retention. Define orphan cleanup and malware scanning adapters. Database and blob backups need a consistent restore strategy.

fields.Vendor evidence: Intacct exposes advanced audit trails. [Advanced audit trails](https://developer.intacct.com/api/company-console/advanced-audit-trails/)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Capture actor/delegation, tenant/company, action, record revision, policy/plugin version and correlation. Audit storage and retention are durable business contracts. Runtime spans/logs supplement them; logs alone do not prove an approved posting or access history.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo documents phased upgrade scripts, unit tests and integration tours. [Upgrades](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/nl/developer/reference/upgrades/upgrade_scripts.html), [Testing](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/developer/reference/backend/testing.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Module compatibility matrix, representative data upgrades, contract tests, role/company isolation tests and posting/reservation race tests. Durable jobs must retain compatible handlers or explicit migration. Restoring code alone cannot roll back a data migration.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo.sh documents backups including filestore and production import. [Odoo.sh operations](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/administration/odoo_sh/getting_started/create.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Define service objectives, tested restore, job recovery, capacity limits, connection budgets, tenant quotas and incident tooling. Alchemy provisions resources; an ERP operations layer owns migration coordination, backup policy and business reconciliation. Choose deployment targets only after persistence and workload requirements.

fields.Vendor evidence: Odoo Community and Enterprise use different licenses; commercial apps can differ again. [Odoo licenses](https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/nl/legal/licenses.html)
fields.Proposed contract or investigation: Record package license/provenance and dependencies in the catalog. Public documentation is capability evidence, not permission to copy proprietary implementations. SAP/Sage product entitlements and adapter access must be checked per product/contract; this index does not establish reusable source rights.

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Supply the application host and API client once to UI Commands and Subscriptions.
fields.Boundary or required work: Runtime resources do not make a dynamically replaced plugin service safe to cache; use leases.

entries.title: Named, schema-argument Commands with result Messages

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Record posting, approval, and install requests as explicit UI operations.
fields.Boundary or required work: A UI success Message is not the authoritative business transaction; return a server result with an operation ID.

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Cancel a report fetch or superseded lookup by request ID.
fields.Boundary or required work: Cancellation cannot undo an already committed posting. Explicitly transition UI pending state on cancellation.

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Follow host state or a filtered activity feed while its screen is open.
fields.Boundary or required work: Host snapshot changes concern availability, not arbitrary domain-data changes. Long leases require coordinated stop.

entries.title: ManagedResource acquire / release from Model conditions

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Own a camera, scanner session, connection, or worker while a feature is mounted.
fields.Boundary or required work: Resource ownership and plugin ownership must agree on stop order; obtaining a bare handle is not a Bridger lease.

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Reuse Effect setup and finalizers in feature-scoped UI resources.
fields.Boundary or required work: Test the combined finalizer order before the resource depends on a removable plugin.

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Host independently loaded plugin screens in shell-owned containers.
fields.Boundary or required work: Establish a teardown acknowledgement before a plugin's required services close.

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Give dynamic screens versioned data contracts without coupling the shell to their private Model.
fields.Boundary or required work: Serialize data, not live services or DOM references; incompatible port versions need explicit rejection or adaptation.

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Compose known screens and reusable UI workflows within one build.
fields.Boundary or required work: A static Message union cannot validate arbitrary future plugin Messages without a separate versioned boundary.

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Attach imperative grids, charts, editors, or scanners to a rendered element.
fields.Boundary or required work: Coordinate DOM cleanup with plugin shutdown; a menu contribution disappearing is not a cleanup acknowledgement.

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Exercise approval forms and command outcomes independently of live ERP services.
fields.Boundary or required work: Add server invariant, authorization, and integration tests; UI stories cannot establish accounting correctness.

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Explain why a screen is waiting, failed, or showing a stale result.
fields.Boundary or required work: Keep sensitive business payloads out of exported histories; debug replay is not a financial audit trail.

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Evaluate public portals or pre-rendered content independently of the back-office application.
fields.Boundary or required work: Official docs mark server rendering experimental; pin and validate build identity, per-request flags, and tenant-sensitive caching.

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Let the shell own routing and page metadata; plugin widgets own only their containers.
fields.Boundary or required work: Multiple independently page-owning applications need an explicit routing and document ownership strategy.

entries.title: Commands and perpetual fibers attached to runtime scope

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Support orderly shutdown of a UI runtime and its ongoing work.
fields.Boundary or required work: Inspect pinned shutdown implementation and test asynchronous finalizers; public disposal completion is still a design check.

fields.ERP / Bridger use: Define a compatible plugin build contract for the browser shell.
fields.Boundary or required work: The observed FoldKit package pins Effect 4.0.0; independently compiled plugins must share compatible framework and service-key identities.

fields.Suggested starting point: Keep dependency resolution, activation, leases, and scoped contribution cleanup in Bridger.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Core examples work without ERP models or a UI framework.

fields.Suggested starting point: Pin a tested Effect / Alchemy / FoldKit tuple and plugin ABI version.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Packages resolve one compatible service-key/runtime graph; upgrades pass compatibility checks.

fields.Suggested starting point: Compare a long-lived process with remote/isolate execution before choosing a deployment target.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Hot loading, restart recovery, tenancy, and resource limits hold in the actual target.

fields.Suggested starting point: Versioned manifest, dependency range, artifact digest, approved entry point, declared host capabilities.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Failed or incompatible loads cannot publish partial providers. Import-time behavior stays constrained by policy.

fields.Suggested starting point: Choose host topology separately from database isolation and company visibility.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Concurrent tenant requests cannot share mutable tenant context, cache entries, or authorization decisions.

fields.Suggested starting point: Central application policy with tenant/company/record/field/action decisions and service identities.
fields.What must be demonstrated: UI, API, background job, import, and report paths enforce the same policy.

fields.Suggested starting point: Define metadata, IDs, relationships, constraints, extension precedence, and schema evolution above core.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Independently installed extensions cannot silently override invariant enforcement or redefine incompatible fields.

fields.Suggested starting point: Expand/contract schema changes, migration history, forward recovery, explicit data retention policy.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Deactivation is safe without dropping schema; old and new code have a tested compatibility window.

fields.Suggested starting point: Place domain state changes and their outbox records in the same database transaction.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Crash tests show no missing committed event and consumers tolerate duplicate delivery.

fields.Suggested starting point: Record workflow definition version, module owner, execution IDs, retry and compensation decisions.
fields.What must be demonstrated: A process survives host restart and a safe plugin upgrade without changing already recorded meaning.

fields.Suggested starting point: Use explicit currencies, units, decimal arithmetic, rounding policy, business dates, and time zones.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Posting and stock examples satisfy domain invariants across currencies and period boundaries.

fields.Suggested starting point: Schema-defined descriptors, versioned ports, activation generations, explicit teardown acknowledgement.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Removing a provider cannot race cleanup code in a still-mounted screen.

fields.Suggested starting point: Separate host lifecycle snapshots from durable domain events and user audit records.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Correlation, retention, ordering scope, and replay semantics are explicit for each stream.

fields.Suggested starting point: Build authorized read models with tenant/company filters and freshness indicators.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Exports and background aggregates cannot bypass field/record policy. Rebuilds are reproducible.

fields.Suggested starting point: Treat migrations, restore drills, disaster recovery, secrets, rollout, and telemetry as product capabilities.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Restore tests recover domain data and in-flight processes into a compatible artifact set.

fields.Suggested starting point: Pick countries, legal entities, industry, and supported business processes before promising parity.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Qualified domain review validates locale-specific posting, tax, payroll, documents, and reporting rules.

fields.Suggested starting point: Prefer keyed registries and explicit extension composition over mutable global patches.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Removing one extension preserves other registrations and their deterministic ordering.

fields.Suggested starting point: ERP runtime roles receive application data permissions; infrastructure mutations use a separate deployment identity.
fields.What must be demonstrated: Disabling a business module cannot trigger accidental destruction of shared infrastructure.

entries.title: `Manifest._from_path` parses manifest literals; `ModuleGraph` resolves installed state, dependencies and ordered phases. Missing dependencies and loops cause modules to be skipped. [module.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/modules/module.py), [module_graph.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/modules/module_graph.py)

fields.Adopt in the ERP platform: Declarative identity, version, owned contributions and prerequisite graph; inspect installation plans before applying them.
fields.Deliberate difference in the Effect desi: Validate JSON-compatible manifest data separately from executing trusted code. Return typed graph errors with dependency paths; do not silently accept a partially applicable installation plan.

entries.title: `Registry` maps model names to classes per database; signaling coordinates registry reloads and cache invalidation across processes. [registry.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/orm/registry.py)

fields.Adopt in the ERP platform: A coherent catalog of installed model definitions and explicit invalidation generations.
fields.Deliberate difference in the Effect desi: Separate durable ERP catalog revisions from Bridger runtime provider generations. A database, tenant and legal company are distinct identities. Publish compatible catalog snapshots rather than mutating existing consumers invisibly.

entries.title: Loading runs migration phases, model/schema setup, data loading and lifecycle hooks; uninstall processes records and rebuilds the registry. [loading.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/modules/loading.py), [migration.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/modules/migration.py)

fields.Adopt in the ERP platform: Dependency-aware install/upgrade planning, migration history, postconditions and explicit uninstall policy.
fields.Deliberate difference in the Effect desi: Define separate artifact import, durable installation, tenant enablement and runtime activation commands. Deactivation releases runtime resources; deleting persistent data requires its own migration/retention operation.

entries.title: `Environment` carries cursor, user, context and superuser mode, plus record cache/recomputation state. [environments.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/orm/environments.py)

fields.Adopt in the ERP platform: Consistent command context and a transaction-bound repository session.
fields.Deliberate difference in the Effect desi: Use typed Effect services for principal, tenant/company, transaction and repositories. Do not pass arbitrary dictionaries as authorization context. Keep transaction-scoped services from escaping their scope.

entries.title: Model classes combine module definitions using Python MRO; field overrides depend on definitions present in the registry. [model_classes.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/orm/model_classes.py)

fields.Adopt in the ERP platform: Modules can extend existing business records and behavior without copying the original module.
fields.Deliberate difference in the Effect desi: Namespaced field contributions and typed hooks with explicit ordering, collision checks and version constraints. Prefer relations/composition over implicit method replacement and `super()` chains across separately installed modules.

entries.title: Fields support computation, inverse/related behavior, dependency and context tracking; stored computed fields default to elevated computation. [fields.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/orm/fields.py)

fields.Adopt in the ERP platform: Declare derived field dependencies, materialization, invalidation and display metadata.
fields.Deliberate difference in the Effect desi: Make execution privilege and transaction policy explicit. Validate dependency graphs and query cost. Wire schemas describe data; adding Effect Schema does not itself create persistence, recomputation or a safe extension ORM.

entries.title: `ir.model.access` grants model CRUD rights; `ir.rule` intersects global domains and unions applicable group domains. [ir_model.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/addons/base/models/ir_model.py), [ir_rule.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/addons/base/models/ir_rule.py)

fields.Adopt in the ERP platform: Separate model/action grants, row restrictions and field visibility. Treat authorization composition as specified behavior.
fields.Deliberate difference in the Effect desi: Define a policy algebra with explicit mandatory tenant/company filters and default denial. Record whether a plugin contributes a grant or restriction. Never let an optional plugin widen mandatory isolation rules.

entries.title: XML/CSV conversion loads records through model APIs, resolves external IDs and supports `noupdate`. [convert.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/tools/convert.py)

fields.Adopt in the ERP platform: Stable namespaced IDs for seed data, menus, views and permissions; reconcile owned definitions on upgrade.
fields.Deliberate difference in the Effect desi: Typed contribution declarations with ownership and explicit replace/preserve policy. Separate developer defaults from customer overrides. Seed installation must be repeatable without duplicating business records.

entries.title: `ir.ui.view` stores view architecture, priority, inheritance and primary/extension modes. [ir_ui_view.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/addons/base/models/ir_ui_view.py)

fields.Adopt in the ERP platform: Metadata-driven forms/lists and third-party extension points.
fields.Deliberate difference in the Effect desi: Use a typed view AST and named slots instead of brittle XPath targeting. Compile validated metadata into FoldKit views; retain custom screens for workflows beyond generated CRUD. UI metadata does not grant server access.

entries.title: Actions carry target model, domain, context and views; menus filter by groups and model read rights. [ir_actions.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/addons/base/models/ir_actions.py), [ir_ui_menu.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/addons/base/models/ir_ui_menu.py)

fields.Adopt in the ERP platform: Stable navigation/action IDs and authorized menu projection.
fields.Deliberate difference in the Effect desi: Distinguish navigation actions from authenticated business commands. Client-visible descriptors contain serializable schemas/references, not database handles or arbitrary server code. FoldKit messages invoke typed command adapters.

entries.title: HTTP handling selects the database registry/environment and authenticates before dispatching an endpoint. [http.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/http.py)

fields.Adopt in the ERP platform: A common ingress path for routing, identity, decoding and error mapping.
fields.Deliberate difference in the Effect desi: Explicit published endpoints and versioned DTOs rather than exposing arbitrary public model methods. Acquire a compatible plugin-generation lease for command execution; recheck authorization inside the business boundary.

entries.title: Request processing retries selected transaction failures; cursors provide commit/rollback callbacks and run postcommit callbacks after SQL commit. [service/model.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/service/model.py), [sql_db.py](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/19.0/odoo/sql_db.py)

fields.Adopt in the ERP platform: Transaction ownership, bounded concurrency retries and clear after-commit semantics.
fields.Deliberate difference in the Effect desi: Persist outbox work in the transaction for durable delivery. Retry the entire valid unit of work only when safe. Effect finalizers handle resource lifetime; they neither reverse committed business facts nor ensure delivery after a crash.
